solution.body:

text: Let $y^{2}=12x$ be the parabola with its vertex at $O$. Let $P$ be a point on the parabola and $A$ be a point on the $x$-axis such that $\angle OPA=90^{\circ }$. Then the locus of the centroid of such triangles $OPA$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

For $y^{2}=12x$, $a=3$. Take $P(3t^{2},6t)$ with $t\neq 0$ and $A(x_{2},0)$.

$\angle OPA=90^{\circ }$ gives $m_{OP}\cdot m_{PA}=-1$:

$\dfrac{6t}{3t^{2}}\times \dfrac{6t}{3t^{2}-x_{2}}=-1\Rightarrow \dfrac{12}{3t^{2}-x_{2}}=-1\Rightarrow x_{2}=3t^{2}+12$

The centroid $(h,k)$ of $O(0,0)$, $P(3t^{2},6t)$ and $A(3t^{2}+12,0)$ is

$h=\dfrac{6t^{2}+12}{3}=2t^{2}+4,k=\dfrac{6t}{3}=2t$

Putting $t=\dfrac{k}{2}$: $h=\dfrac{k^{2}}{2}+4\Rightarrow k^{2}-2h+8=0$.

So the locus is $y^{2}-2x+8=0$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
If the system of equations

 $3x+y+4z=3$ 

 $2x+αy-z=-3$ 

 $x+2y+z=4$ 

has no solution, then the value of $α$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A system with no solution must have a vanishing coefficient determinant:

$\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & 1 & 4 \\ 2 & α & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \end{array}\right |=3(α+2)-1(2+1)+4(4-α)=19-α.$

For $α\neq 19$, $\Delta \neq 0$ and the system has a unique solution, so $α=19$ is the only candidate.

For $α=19$, replacing the $x$-column by the constants,

$\Delta _{1}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & 1 & 4 \\ -3 & 19 & -1 \\ 4 & 2 & 1 \end{array}\right |=3(19+2)-1(-3+4)+4(-6-76)=63-1-328=-266\neq 0,$

so with $\Delta =0$ and $\Delta _{1}\neq 0$ the system is inconsistent and $α=19$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$|z-5|\leq 3$ is the closed disc with centre $C(5,0)$ and radius 3. The point of the disc with the largest positive argument is the point of contact $P$ of the tangent from the origin $O$ to the upper half of the circle.

In the right triangle $OPC$, $OC=5$ and $CP=3$, so $OP=4$, $\sin θ=\dfrac{3}{5}$ and $\cos θ=\dfrac{4}{5}$.


[IMG]

$z=4(\cos θ+i\sin θ)=4\left (\dfrac{4}{5}+\dfrac{3}{5}i\right )=\dfrac{16+12i}{5}\Rightarrow 5z=16+12i$

$5z-12=4+12i,5iz+16=i(16+12i)+16=4+16i$

$\left |\dfrac{5z-12}{5iz+16}\right |^{2}=\dfrac{4^{2}+12^{2}}{4^{2}+16^{2}}=\dfrac{160}{272}=\dfrac{10}{17}$

$34\times \dfrac{10}{17}=20$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
The positive integer n, for which the solutions of the equation 
$x(x+2)+(x+2)(x+4)+\cdots +(x+2n-2)(x+2n)=\frac{8n}{3}$ are two consecutive even integers, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The left-hand side contains $n$ terms:

$\sum\limits _{k=0}^{n-1}(x+2k)(x+2k+2)$

Expanding one term,

$(x+2k)(x+2k+2)=x^{2}+(4k+2)x+4k(k+1)$

Using the standard sums, the equation becomes

$nx^{2}+2n^{2}x+\frac{4n(n^{2}-1)}{3}=\frac{8n}{3}$

Since $n$ is positive, divide by $n$:

$x^{2}+2nx+\frac{4n^{2}-12}{3}=0$

The two roots are consecutive even integers, so their difference is $2$. For a quadratic $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$, the difference between its roots is

$\frac{\sqrt{D}}{|a|}$

Here $a=1$, so $\sqrt{D}=2$, giving $D=4$.

Now,

$D=(2n)^{2}-4\left (\frac{4n^{2}-12}{3}\right )$

$4=4n^{2}-\frac{16n^{2}-48}{3}$

$4=16-\frac{4n^{2}}{3}$

$\frac{4n^{2}}{3}=12$

$n^{2}=9$

As $n$ is positive,

$n=3$

For $n=3$, the roots are $-4$ and $-2$, which are consecutive even integers.

Hence, the correct option is Option A: $3$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift

solution.body:
For set $A$, we have the inequality:

$|x^{2}-10|\leq 6$

This means that the expression inside the modulus lies between $-6$ and $6$:

$-6\leq x^{2}-10\leq 6$

By adding $10$ to all parts of the inequality, we get:

$4\leq x^{2}\leq 16$

Taking the square root gives us the range for $|x|$:

$2\leq |x|\leq 4$

This tells us that the value of $x$ can be positive or negative, giving us the intervals:

$A=[-4,-2]\cup [2,4]$

Now, let's find the elements of set $B$ from its inequality:

$|x-2|>1$

This breaks down into two conditions:

$x-2<-1\text{or}x-2>1$

Solving these, we get:

$x<1\text{or}x>3$

Writing this in interval notation, we have:

$B=(-\infty ,1)\cup (3,\infty )$

Now we check the options by performing the set operations. Let's find $B-A$, which represents the elements present in $B$ but not in $A$. 

We take the set $B$ and remove any overlapping parts from $A$. 

Looking at the first part of $B$, which is $(-\infty ,1)$, we need to remove the interval $[-4,-2]$ that belongs to $A$. Since the endpoints $-4$ and $-2$ are in $A$, they will be removed, leaving open brackets. This breaks the remaining interval into:

$(-\infty ,-4)\cup (-2,1)$

Next, looking at the second part of $B$, which is $(3,\infty )$, we need to remove the elements from $A$ that overlap here. The set $A$ contains $[2,4]$. Removing this portion from $(3,\infty )$ cuts off everything up to $4$. Since $4$ is in $A$, it is removed, so we use an open bracket starting from $4$:

$(4,\infty )$

Combining these remaining parts together, we get:

$B-A=(-\infty ,-4)\cup (-2,1)\cup (4,\infty )$

This exactly matches Option B. 

Option B is the correct choice.

solution.body:

text:
Let $f:\mathrm{ℝ}\to \mathrm{ℝ}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f^{''}(x)>0$ for all $x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ and $f^{'}(a-1)=0$, where $a$ is a real number.

 Let $g(x)=f(\tan ^{2}x-2\tan x+a),0<x<\frac{π}{2}$.

Consider the following two statements:

(I) g is increasing in $\left (0,\frac{π}{4}\right )$

(II) g is decreasing in $\left (\frac{π}{4},\frac{π}{2}\right )$

Then,
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\tan ^{2}x-2\tan x+a=(\tan x-1)^{2}+(a-1)$, $g(x)=f\left ((\tan x-1)^{2}+a-1\right )$ and

$g^{'}(x)=f^{'}\left ((\tan x-1)^{2}+a-1\right )\cdot 2(\tan x-1)\sec ^{2}x$

As $f^{''}(x)>0$ for all $x$, $f^{'}$ is strictly increasing. For $x\neq \dfrac{π}{4}$, $(\tan x-1)^{2}>0$, so $(\tan x-1)^{2}+a-1>a-1$ and

$f^{'}\left ((\tan x-1)^{2}+a-1\right )>f^{'}(a-1)=0$

With $\sec ^{2}x>0$, the sign of $g^{'}(x)$ is the sign of $\tan x-1$.

For $0<x<\dfrac{π}{4}$, $\tan x<1$, so $g^{'}(x)<0$ and $g$ is decreasing in $\left (0,\dfrac{π}{4}\right )$: statement (I) is false.

For $\dfrac{π}{4}<x<\dfrac{π}{2}$, $\tan x>1$, so $g^{'}(x)>0$ and $g$ is increasing in $\left (\dfrac{π}{4},\dfrac{π}{2}\right )$: statement (II) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift

text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\sec x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-2y=2+3\sin x$, $x\in \left (-\dfrac{π}{2},\dfrac{π}{2}\right )$,
$y(0)=-\dfrac{7}{4}$. Then $y\left (\dfrac{π}{6}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Multiplying the equation by $\cos x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}-2\cos x\cdot y=\cos x(2+3\sin x)$

The integrating factor is $e^{-\int 2\cos xdx}=e^{-2\sin x}$, so

$y~e^{-2\sin x}=\int e^{-2\sin x}\cos x(2+3\sin x)dx$

Putting $\sin x=t$, $\cos x\qquad dx=dt$ and integrating by parts:

$\int (2+3t)e^{-2t}dt=-\dfrac{(2+3t)e^{-2t}}{2}+\dfrac{3}{2}\int e^{-2t}dt=-\dfrac{(2+3t)e^{-2t}}{2}-\dfrac{3}{4}e^{-2t}+C$

Dividing by $e^{-2\sin x}$:

$y=-\dfrac{2+3\sin x}{2}-\dfrac{3}{4}+Ce^{2\sin x}$

At $x=0$: $-\dfrac{7}{4}=-1-\dfrac{3}{4}+C$, so $C=0$.

At $x=\dfrac{π}{6}$, $\sin x=\dfrac{1}{2}$:

$y\left (\dfrac{π}{6}\right )=-\dfrac{7}{4}-\dfrac{3}{4}=-\dfrac{5}{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift

solution.body: $\begin{array}{lllll} A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 3 & -4 \\ 1 & -1 \end{array}\right ],B=\left [\begin{array}{ll} -29 & 49 \\ -13 & 18 \end{array}\right ] \\ \text{Characteristic equation of A,} \\ \begin{array}{lll} (3-λ)(-1-λ)+4=0 \\ (λ-3)(λ+1)+4=λ^{2}-2λ+1=0 \\ \Rightarrow A^{2}-2A+I=0 \\ A^{2}=2A-I,A^{3}=2A^{2}-A=2(2A-I)-A=3A-2I \\ A^{4}=4A^{2}+I-4A=4(2A-I)-4A+I=4A-3I \\ A^{5}=4A^{2}-3A=4(2A-I)-3A=5A-4I \\ \left (A^{5}\right )^{3}=(5A-4I)^{3} \\ =125A^{3}-3\times 25A^{2}(4)+3(5A)\left (4^{2}\right )-64I \\ =125(3A-2I)-300(2A-I)+240A-64I \\ =A(375-600+240)+I(-250+300-64) \\ =15A-14I \\ \Rightarrow A^{15}+B=15A-14I+B \\ =\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & -11 \\ 2 & -11 \end{array}\right ]\left (A^{15}+B\right )\left [\begin{array}{l} x \\ y \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow 2x=11y \end{array} \end{array}$

text:
A random variable X takes values 0, 1, 2, 3 with probabilities $\frac{2a+1}{30}$, $\frac{8a-1}{30}$, $\frac{4a+1}{30}$, $b$ respectively, where $a,b\in \mathrm{ℝ}$. 

Let $μ$ and $σ$ respectively be the mean and standard deviation of $X$ such that $σ^{2}+μ^{2}=2$.
Then $\frac{a}{b}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The probabilities add to 1:

$\frac{(2a+1)+(8a-1)+(4a+1)}{30}+b=1\Rightarrow 14a+30b=29\text{(i)}$

Since $σ^{2}=E(X^{2})-μ^{2}$, the condition $σ^{2}+μ^{2}=2$ means $E(X^{2})=2$:

$1^{2}\cdot \frac{8a-1}{30}+2^{2}\cdot \frac{4a+1}{30}+3^{2}\cdot b=2\Rightarrow 24a+3+270b=60\Rightarrow 8a+90b=19\text{(ii)}$

Three times (i) gives $42a+90b=87$; subtracting (ii) gives $34a=68$, so $a=2$, and then $30b=29-28$, so $b=\dfrac{1}{30}$. The probabilities $\dfrac{5}{30},\dfrac{15}{30},\dfrac{9}{30},\dfrac{1}{30}$ are all valid.

$\frac{a}{b}=2\times 30=60$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift

text: The largest $n\in \mathrm{ℕ}$, for which $7^{n}$ divides $101!$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\text{Exponent of}7\text{in}101!=\left [\frac{101}{7}\right ]+\left [\frac{101}{7^{2}}\right ]+\ldots ..\text{(Where [.] is G.I.F.)}=14+2=16$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift

text: Let the line $L_{1}$ be parallel to the vector $-3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ and pass through the point $(2,6,7)$, and the line $L_{2}$ be parallel to the vector $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and pass through the point $(4,3,5)$. If the line $L_{3}$ is parallel to the vector $-3\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+16\hat{k}$ and intersects the lines $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ at the points $C$ and $D$, respectively, then $\left |CD\leftarrow \right |^{2}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} L_{1}:\dfrac{x-2}{-3}=\dfrac{y-6}{2}=\dfrac{z-7}{4}=t \\ L_{2}:\dfrac{x-4}{2}=\dfrac{y-3}{1}=\dfrac{z-5}{3}=s \end{array}$

Any point on $L_{1}$ is $C=(-3t+2,2t+6,4t+7)$

Any point on $L_{2}$ is $D=(2s+4,s+3,3s+5)$

d.r's of $CD\leftarrow =(2s+3t+2,s-2t-3,3s-4t-2)$

CD is parallel to $-3i+5j+16k$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{2s+3t+2}{-3}=\dfrac{s-2t-3}{5}=\dfrac{3s-4t-2}{16} \\ 13s+9t+1=0\ldots .(i) \\ 41s+36t+26=0\ldots .(2) \end{array}$

Solve (i) \& (2) $s=2;t=-3$

$\begin{array}{l} C=(11,0,-5) \\ D=(8,5,11) \\ CD^{2}=290 \end{array}$

text: Let $[\cdot ]$ denote the greatest integer function and $f(x)=\lim _{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{n^{3}}\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\left [\frac{k^{2}}{3^{x}}\right ]$. Then $12\sum\limits _{j=1}^{\infty }f(j)$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} f(x)=\lim _{n\to \infty }\left (\dfrac{1}{n^{3}}\cdot \sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\left [\dfrac{k^{2}}{3^{x}}\right ]\right )=\lim _{n\to \infty }\dfrac{1}{n^{3}}\cdot \sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\left (\dfrac{k^{2}}{3^{x}}\right )-\lim _{n\to \infty }\dfrac{1}{n^{3}}\cdot \sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\left \{\dfrac{k^{2}}{3^{x}}\right \} \\ f(x)=\lim _{n\to \infty }\dfrac{1}{n^{3}}\times \dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6\times 3^{x}}-0\Rightarrow f(x)=\dfrac{1}{3^{x+1}} \\ 12\sum\limits _{j=1}^{\infty }f(j)=12\left (\dfrac{1}{3^{2}}+\dfrac{1}{3^{3}}+\dfrac{1}{3^{4}}+\ldots .\right )=12\left (\dfrac{\frac{1}{9}}{1-\frac{1}{3}}\right )=\dfrac{12}{9-3}=2 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift

text: If $P$ is a point on the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=4,Q$ is a point on the straight line $5x+y+2=0$ and $x-y+1=0$ is the perpendicular bisector of PQ , then 13 times the sum of abscissa of all such points P is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$P(x_{1},y_{1})$ and point $Q(x_{2},y_{2})$

Mid point of $\mathrm{PQ}M=\left (\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}}{2},\frac{y_{1}+y_{2}}{2}\right )$

Substitute M into $x-y+1=0$

$x_{1}+x_{2}-y_{1}-y_{2}+2=0..(i)$

Slope of PQ is Perpendicular to slope of bisector line So, slope of $PQ=-1$

$y_{2}=x_{1}-x_{2}+y_{1}\ldots ..(ii)$

$Q(x_{2},y_{2})$ lie on $5x+y+2=0$

So, $5x_{2}+y_{2}+2=0\ldots \ldots$. (iii)

Substitute (ii) in (iii)

$x_{2}=\frac{-x_{1}-y_{1}-2}{4}\ldots .(iv)$

Substitute (ii) in (i)

$x_{2}=y_{1}-1\ldots ..(v)$

From (iv) and (v)

$x_{1}=2-5y_{1}$

$(x_{1},y_{1})$ lie on circle

$x_{1}^{2}+y_{1}^{2}=4$

Put $x_{1}=2-5y_{1}$

$y_{1}=0,\frac{10}{13}$

So, $x_{1}=2,\frac{-24}{13}$

So, $2+\left (-\frac{24}{13}\right )=\frac{2}{13}$

So, $13\times \frac{2}{13}=2$

text:
If $\left (\frac{1}{{}^{15}\mathrm{C}_{0}}+\frac{1}{{}^{15}\mathrm{C}_{1}}\right )\left (\frac{1}{{}^{15}\mathrm{C}_{1}}+\frac{1}{{}^{15}\mathrm{C}_{2}}\right )\ldots \left (\frac{1}{{}^{15}\mathrm{C}_{12}}+\frac{1}{{}^{15}\mathrm{C}_{13}}\right )=\frac{α^{13}}{{}^{14}\mathrm{C}_{0}{}^{14}\mathrm{C}_{1}\cdots {}^{14}\mathrm{C}_{12}}$, then $30α$ is equal to
$____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{1}{{}^{n}C_{r}}+\dfrac{1}{{}^{n}C_{r+1}}=\dfrac{{}^{n}C_{r+1}+{}^{n}C_{r}}{{}^{n}C_{r}\cdot {}^{n}C_{r+1}}=\dfrac{{}^{n+1}C_{r+1}}{{}^{n}C_{r}\cdot {}^{n}C_{r+1}}=\dfrac{\frac{n+1}{r+1}\cdot {}^{n}C_{r}}{{}^{n}C_{r}\cdot {}^{n}C_{r+1}}=\dfrac{(n+1)}{(r+1)\cdot \frac{n}{r+1}\cdot {}^{n-1}C_{r}}=\dfrac{n+1}{n\cdot {}^{n-1}C_{r}} \\ \therefore \left (\dfrac{1}{15C_{0}}+\dfrac{1}{15C_{1}}\right )\left (\dfrac{1}{15C_{1}}+\dfrac{1}{15C_{2}}\right )\cdots \left (\dfrac{1}{15C_{12}}+\dfrac{1}{15C_{13}}\right )=\dfrac{16}{15\cdot {}^{14}C_{0}}\cdot \dfrac{16}{15\cdot {}^{14}C_{1}}\cdot \dfrac{16}{15\cdot {}^{14}C_{12}}=\dfrac{\left (\frac{16}{15}\right )^{13}}{{}^{14}C_{0}\cdot {}^{14}C_{1}\cdot {}^{14}C_{2}\cdot \cdots {}^{14}C_{12}} \\ \therefore α=\dfrac{16}{15} \\ \therefore 30α=32 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift

text: If $\int\limits _{0}^{1}4\cot ^{-1}\left (1-2x+4x^{2}\right )\mathrm{d}x=\mathrm{a}~\tan ^{-1}(2)-\mathrm{b}\log _{\mathrm{e}}(5)$, where $\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b}\in \mathrm{N}$, then $(2\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b})$ is equal to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We are given  

$\int\limits _{0}^{1}4\cot ^{-1}(1-2x+4x^{2})dx=a\tan ^{-1}(2)-b\ln (5),a,b\in \mathrm{ℕ}$

Step 1: Simplify the integrand
$1-2x+4x^{2}=4x^{2}-2x+1>0\forall x\in [0,1]$

For positive arguments,

$\cot ^{-1}(u)=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{u}\right )$

so

$\int\limits _{0}^{1}4\cot ^{-1}(4x^{2}-2x+1)dx=4\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{4x^{2}-2x+1}\right )dx$

Using the identity $\tan ^{-1}(1/u)=\frac{π}{2}-\tan ^{-1}(u)$ (for $u>0$):

$=4\left [\frac{π}{2}-\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}(4x^{2}-2x+1)dx\right ]$

Step 2: Evaluate the remaining integral
Using integration by parts and standard integrals of rational functions, one obtains:

$\int\limits _{0}^{1}\tan ^{-1}(4x^{2}-2x+1)dx=\tan ^{-1}(3)-\frac{1}{4}\ln 5$

Substitute back:

$\begin{array}{ll} I & =4\left [\dfrac{π}{2}-\tan ^{-1}(3)+\dfrac{1}{4}\ln 5\right ] \\ =4\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1}{3}\right )+\ln 5 \end{array}$

Using the identity:

$\tan ^{-1}(2)=2\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{3}\right )$

we get:

$I=4\tan ^{-1}(2)-\ln 5$

Step 3: Identify $a$ and $b$
Comparing with  

$a\tan ^{-1}(2)-b\ln (5)$

we have:

$a=4,b=1$

Final Answer
$2a+b=2(4)+1=9$

text: Let the maximum value of $\left (\sin ^{-1}x\right )^{2}+\left (\cos ^{-1}x\right )^{2}$ for $x\in \left [-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$ be $\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{n}}π^{2}$, where $\gcd (\mathrm{m},\mathrm{n})=1$. Then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to $____$。
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\left (\sin ^{-1}x\right )^{2}+\left (\cos ^{-1}x\right )^{2},x\in \left [-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$

For $x\in [-1,1]$,

$\sin ^{-1}x+\cos ^{-1}x=\frac{π}{2}.$

Let $a=\sin ^{-1}x$. Then $\cos ^{-1}x=\frac{π}{2}-a$, and

$f=a^{2}+\left (\frac{π}{2}-a\right )^{2}=2a^{2}-πa+\frac{π^{2}}{4}.$

This is a quadratic in $a$ opening upward, so its maximum on the allowed interval occurs at an endpoint of $a$.

Now,

$x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\Rightarrow a=-\frac{π}{3},x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\Rightarrow a=\frac{π}{4}.$

Evaluate $f$:

At $a=\frac{π}{4}$: this is the vertex, giving the minimum.

At $a=-\frac{π}{3}$:

$f=\left (-\frac{π}{3}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{5π}{6}\right )^{2}=\frac{π^{2}}{9}+\frac{25π^{2}}{36}=\frac{29π^{2}}{36}.$

Hence the maximum value is

$\frac{m}{n}π^{2}=\frac{29}{36}π^{2},$

with $\gcd (29,36)=1$.

$m+n=65$
